title: Batching & latency
evidenceStatus: 120 serial requests across 12 repeated-question payloads; 118 completed, with 169 transport attempts and one positive semantic fact.
summary: The sweep shows that a request can return many copies of one easy Noul judgment, but it does not measure useful decision throughput. Its successful-only p95 hides failed-request waiting: one group's displayed 3.38-second p95 becomes 9.09 seconds when all terminal durations are counted. A paired, independently labelled workload and a queue replay would make the batching tradeoff measurable.
strengths: All 12 published percentile pairs reproduce from the recorded successful rows, and failure durations remain available.
The client validates every expected answer and records retry-aware evaluate duration separately from successful-attempt timing.
The published transport summary distinguishes attempts, logical requests, HTTP errors, and missing cost metadata.
Five relevant Python contract tests pass; raw local logs contain all 5,030 returned question slots.

findings.title: Repeated copies of one positive question do not measure useful batching
findings.evidence: jev-experiments/src/jev_lab/benchmarks.py:220-239; probe found 12 payload hashes, one instruction, 5,030 returned slots, and actual state lengths of 109/1,009/4,009 words.
findings.impact: The current run measures repetitive payload timing and acceptance. It cannot establish independent decision quality, diverse-question scaling, or correctness when multiple records share a packed state.
findings.fix: Retain the current condition as a transport control. Add balanced distinct labels, predictions, stable question IDs, tokens and bytes, and separate same-state fan-out from multiple-record packing.

findings.title: Successful-only p95 hides failed waiting
findings.evidence: jev-experiments/src/jev_lab/benchmarks.py:256-268; results/latency.jsonl:11 shows 3,378ms p95 for nine successes; the omitted tenth request failed after 12,815ms, producing 9,085ms p95 across all terminal durations.
findings.impact: A condition can look faster because a slow request fails. Terminal duration also must not be confused with time to a valid decision.
findings.fix: Show success-conditional latency, all-request terminal duration, failure rate, and correct decisions delivered before the deadline as separate metrics, with all offered work retained in availability denominators.

findings.title: Serial fixed-order samples confound packing with service conditions
findings.evidence: jev-experiments/src/jev_lab/benchmarks.py:220-252 awaits each request; core.py:255-258 reuses one HTTP client; local log maximum in flight is one; 43 of 120 requests retry; each group has only ten samples.
findings.impact: The experiment cannot isolate request concurrency, cold-client effects, provider coldness, cache behavior, or sustainable capacity. Time-varying gateway pressure can explain group differences.
findings.fix: Use randomized paired blocks, explicit concurrency and arrival schedules, an isolated ledger, labelled warm-up and fresh-client diagnostics, and timing stages for local queue, attempts and backoff. Keep provider coldness unknown without evidence.

findings.title: The comparison lacks an equal-work baseline and useful throughput
findings.evidence: jev-experiments/experience-prototypes/src/benchmarks.tsx:553-564 shows request medians and request counts; results/latency.jsonl:9 represents ten requests carrying 1,280 answer slots.
findings.impact: A fast packed request does not establish a better time to useful decisions. Dividing duration by question count would omit shared response waiting and any batch-collection delay.
findings.fix: Compare identical labelled work through serial singleton calls, bounded concurrent singleton calls, and native multi-question calls. Measure job completion and correct on-time decisions per elapsed second.

findings.title: The chart clips slow medians and turns empty percentiles into zero
findings.evidence: jev-experiments/experience-prototypes/src/benchmarks.tsx:558 caps bars at 1,500ms; the 4,000/32 condition has a 1,670ms median. Lines 561-563 pass nullable percentiles to Math.round, which coerces null to zero.
findings.impact: The visual suppresses the latency tail and would imply instant success for a group with no successful requests.
findings.fix: Use a labelled shared scale, distributions or request dots with failure marks, explicit no-success states, and selectable request timelines.

findings.title: Cost and version metadata do not support a durable efficiency claim
findings.evidence: jev-experiments/results/latency.jsonl:1 reports $0 and 51 attempts without cost metadata; lines 134-136 contain cumulative 3,500-attempt ledger totals. Local successful responses identify only typesafe-ai/jev.
findings.impact: A promotional price and cross-run ledger totals cannot establish run-specific steady-state cost; the underlying model version remains unknown.
findings.fix: Record run-local tokens, billed cost, missing-cost counts, route, exposed model identity, and dated pricing sources. Separate promotional price, estimates and measured bills, and preserve unknown fields.

simulation.title: A support desk under load
simulation.description: Replay one seeded ticket arrival stream through singleton dispatch, immediate packing, and 25/100ms collection windows. Let visitors vary question cap, request concurrency and a two-second target, then inspect each ticket's collection wait, queue, attempts, backoff and final disposition.
simulation.jevsRole: Judge ticket intent and urgency against a frozen rubric, returning values tied to stable ticket/question IDs and state revisions.
simulation.codeRole: Create shared states, enforce packing limits, schedule and retry requests, validate answers, handle deadlines, score independent outcomes, and generate a deterministic replay. Counterfactual scheduling uses labelled simulations, not invented model measurements.
acceptanceCriteria: The same seed reproduces arrival timestamps and scheduler events.
Every result maps to its original ticket, question, state revision and request; stale or missing values cannot silently complete work.
Collection windows and capacity queues are displayed separately.
Every policy receives identical offered work, and failed, expired and dropped work remains in all service-target denominators.
Timeline stages reconcile to measured end-to-end duration and distinguish request latency from ticket waiting.
Recorded replay makes zero model requests; unsupported load conditions cannot borrow an optimistic serial timing estimate.

evaluation.design: Use 20 development and 100 held-out scene seeds, each with 128 distinct balanced statements and three token-length variants. Freeze labels and templates independently of Jev. Run every held-out bundle with pack sizes 1/8/32/128 and concurrency caps 1/4 in five randomized time blocks: 89,400 logical requests. Add 9,000 tail-extension requests and 100 labelled warm-ups for 98,500 total, with at most 295,500 attempts under the three-attempt rule. Use a dedicated reviewed ledger because the existing 10,000-attempt cap is insufficient. Report paired 95% intervals clustered by scene seed and block; lengths are correlated. Offline scheduler checks cover 30 arrival seeds x 3 profiles x 3 policies x 3 concurrency caps = 810 simulations. Packing succeeds only when the paired 95% goodput-ratio interval exceeds 1, the 95% upper correctness-loss bound is below one percentage point, and 99% of offered decisions are correct within two seconds. No such run was performed in this audit.
baselines: Singleton requests with concurrency one for the same 128-question workset.
Singleton requests with concurrency four for the same workset.
Native packs of 8, 32 and 128 questions under the same arrival stream and concurrency budget.
A deterministic fact oracle for scorer and scheduler validation, plus always-true as a label-balance check.
metrics: Request p50/p95 with sample counts and uncertainty, reported separately for successful and all terminal outcomes.
Batch collection wait, local admission wait, attempt duration, retry wait, full workset completion and retry count.
Request availability, decision availability, and semantic accuracy conditional on returned values.
Correct decisions delivered within two seconds / all offered decisions, and correct on-time decisions / elapsed wall-clock seconds.
Run-local input tokens and billed versus estimated cost per 1,000 correct on-time decisions, with unknown-cost coverage.
Achieved concurrency, actual versus offered arrival rate, dropped arrivals, payload bytes, version/route metadata and content-reuse status.

coverage.current: One positive semantic fact; 12 payload configurations x 10 serial requests = 120 requests, 118 completed. All 5,030 returned question slots repeat the same instruction.
coverage.full: Proposed authored held-out coverage is 100 scene seeds x 3 token-length variants x 128 distinct questions = 38,400 instances in 300 state bundles. Full paired transport plan is 98,500 logical requests including tail extensions and 100 warm-ups. There is no external split or official leaderboard score for this systems benchmark.
coverage.feasibility: No large dataset or weights are required. Current gateway promotional pricing favors complete coverage, but the run needs an isolated budget above the default cap, provider-respecting pacing, checkpointing and adequate time. Gateway errors, opaque model version, route-specific limits, and missing failed-attempt costs remain confounds. Run the scorer and scheduler offline first; a transport preflight cannot replace full evaluation.

libraries.name: Grafana k6
libraries.use: Drive the later live arrival-rate test independently of service completion; retain error and dropped-iteration metrics alongside custom correct-decision outcomes.

libraries.name: SimPy
libraries.use: Simulate collection windows, finite request capacity, deadlines, outages and backoff deterministically, then export replay events to React.

nextSteps.action: Correct count labels, expose failed waits and retries, handle empty percentiles, and fix axis clipping while retaining the existing transport-control evidence.
Retain distinct labelled answers, token lengths, IDs, timing stages and run-local cost/version metadata; add regression cases for failure-only and mixed-result groups.
Implement the randomized paired runner with explicit concurrency, a dedicated budget ledger, checkpoints and the published complete-coverage plan.
Build the support-desk replay and validate 810 offline scheduler simulations.
Extend to multiple-record packing and live arrival-rate measurement; reuse the scheduler for semantic-table scans, routing and deadline-aware fallback.
